column3: Chemicals in sunscreen are worse for you than a sunburn.
column13: run 1: aad-sunscreen-safety + aad-cloudy-days; run 2: aad-sunscreen-safety + aad-cloudy-days; run 3: aad-sunscreen-safety + aad-cloudy-days
column15: The claim says the chemicals in sunscreen are more harmful to your health than getting a sunburn.
column16: Dermatology guidance says people should keep using sunscreen, and the FDA has not concluded that any sunscreen ingredients sold in the U.S. are unsafe. Sunburn is a sign of UV damage to skin, and UV can reach your skin even on cloudy days. Comparing the two as if sunscreen were the bigger risk reverses what the evidence shows.

column3: You don't need sunscreen on cloudy days.
column13: run 1: aad-cloudy-days; run 2: aad-cloudy-days; run 3: aad-cloudy-days
column15: Sunscreen is unnecessary on cloudy days.
column16: Clouds block some visible light but not most UV rays. Dermatology guidance says up to 80% of UV rays can penetrate your skin on cloudy days, so skin can still be exposed to sun damage when the sky looks gray.

column3: Darker skin tones don't need sunscreen.
column9: Absolute language; One size fits all
column13: run 1: aad-cloudy-days + aad-sunscreen-safety; run 2: aad-cloudy-days + aad-sunscreen-safety; run 3: aad-cloudy-days + aad-sunscreen-safety
column15: People with darker skin tones do not need to wear sunscreen.
column16: More melanin gives some natural protection from UV, but it does not remove the risk of sun damage or skin cancer. UV rays reach the skin in every skin tone, and up to 80% of UV rays can penetrate skin even on cloudy days. Skin cancers in darker skin are often found later, which can make them harder to treat.

column3: Put toothpaste on a pimple overnight to dry it out.
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Applying toothpaste to a pimple overnight will dry it out and help it clear.
column16: Dermatology guidance does not recommend toothpaste for acne. Toothpaste is made for teeth, and ingredients like detergents, flavorings and whiteners can irritate or burn skin, which may leave redness, peeling or dark marks that last longer than the pimple. Drying a spot out also does not treat what causes it, and no vetted source on file covers this claim directly.

column3: Rub lemon juice on dark spots to fade them.
column13: run 1: aad-cloudy-days; run 2: aad-cloudy-days; run 3: aad-cloudy-days
column15: Rubbing lemon juice on dark spots will fade them.
column16: Lemon juice is acidic and can irritate or burn skin, and sun exposure afterward can make dark spots look worse. Dermatology guidance does not recommend it for fading discoloration, and there is no good evidence that it works. Dark spots have different causes, so a single home fix is unlikely to suit everyone.

column3: If you use a retinoid, wear sunscreen every day.
column13: run 1: aad-cloudy-days + aad-sunscreen-safety; run 2: aad-cloudy-days + aad-sunscreen-safety; run 3: aad-cloudy-days + aad-sunscreen-safety
column15: Anyone who uses a retinoid on their skin should also wear sunscreen every day.
column16: Dermatology guidance recommends daily sunscreen for most people, and it matters more with retinoids because they can make skin more sensitive to sun. UV rays also reach your skin on cloudy days, so daily use makes sense even when the sky looks gray. Regulators have not found the sunscreen ingredients sold in the U.S. to be unsafe.

column3: Beef tallow is the best moisturizer for every skin type.
column9: Absolute language; One size fits all
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Beef tallow is the single best moisturizer for every skin type.
column16: Skin types differ, so no single moisturizer is best for everyone. Dermatology guidance does not recommend animal fat as a universal moisturizer, and people with oily or acne-prone skin may find heavy fats clog pores or worsen breakouts. Some people may like how it feels, but the claim that it is best for every skin type goes well beyond the evidence.

column3: Detox teas flush toxins out of your liver.
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Detox teas remove toxins from your liver.
column16: Your liver and kidneys already filter and clear waste on their own, and no good evidence shows that a tea speeds up or improves this. Many of these teas work mainly as laxatives or diuretics, so any change on the scale or in your gut is temporary fluid loss, not toxins leaving the liver. The word toxins is rarely defined, which makes the claim hard to test.

column3: Most adults need at least 7 hours of sleep a night.
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Most adults need at least 7 hours of sleep each night.
column16: Major sleep and public health guidance recommends that adults get 7 or more hours of sleep per night on a regular basis. Regularly sleeping less is linked with worse health and alertness. Needs vary a little from person to person, and the claim says most adults, which fits that.

column3: If you don't hit 10,000 steps, walking doesn't count.
column9: Absolute language; One size fits all
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Walking only counts as exercise or gives health benefits if you reach 10,000 steps in a day.
column16: Health benefits from walking begin well below 10,000 steps and keep growing as you add more. The 10,000 figure is a round number that became popular, not a cutoff where benefits start. Public health guidance focuses on regular moderate activity over the week, so shorter walks still count.

column3: Strength training twice a week is good for long-term health.
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Doing strength training two times a week supports your long-term health.
column16: Public health and medical guidelines recommend muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days a week for adults. It is linked with better muscle and bone strength, better blood sugar control, and healthier aging. The claim is modest and does not promise a dramatic result.

column3: Cold plunges cure anxiety.
column9: Miracle claim; Absolute language; One size fits all
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Cold plunges, meaning immersion in very cold water, cure anxiety.
column16: Small studies suggest cold water exposure may lift mood for a short time in some people, but there is no good evidence that it cures an anxiety disorder. Medical and mental health guidance relies on treatments such as therapy and, when appropriate, medication. Cold water also strains the heart and breathing, so it carries real risks for some people.

column3: Taping your mouth shut at night fixes sleep for everyone.
column9: Absolute language; One size fits all; Miracle claim
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Taping your mouth shut at night improves sleep for every person.
column16: Sleep problems have many causes, and no mainstream sleep or medical guidance says mouth taping fixes sleep for everyone. Research on it is very limited, and covering the mouth can be unsafe for people with a blocked nose, breathing problems or sleep apnea, because it may make breathing harder.

column3: This coin is guaranteed to 10x by next month. Get in before it's too late.
column9: Guaranteed results; Urgency; Unrealistic income; Fear-based
column13: run 1: sec-crypto-guaranteed-returns; run 2: sec-crypto-guaranteed-returns; run 3: sec-crypto-guaranteed-returns
column15: A crypto coin is guaranteed to increase tenfold in value within a month, and you should buy in now before the chance passes.
column16: No investment can guarantee a return, and a promise of very high gains with little or no risk is a classic warning sign of fraud. Prices of speculative assets can fall as easily as they rise, so a fixed outcome in a fixed time cannot be known in advance. The pressure to act before it is too late is meant to rush your thinking.

column3: Checking your own credit score lowers it.
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Looking at your own credit score or report will cause your credit score to go down.
column16: Checking your own score or report is generally treated as a soft inquiry, which does not count against you in standard scoring. Hard inquiries, which can cause a small and temporary dip, happen when a lender reviews your credit because you applied for new credit. Regular self-checks are widely encouraged so you can catch errors or signs of identity theft early.

column3: Buy now, pay later is basically free money.
column9: Absolute language; One size fits all
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Buy now, pay later plans are described as basically free money, as if using them costs nothing.
column16: Some buy now, pay later plans charge no interest when every payment is made on time, so the claim has a small kernel of truth. Late fees, missed payments, or a plan that converts to interest-bearing credit can make it cost real money, and splitting purchases into small payments can make it easier to spend more than you planned. Terms differ from plan to plan, so the answer depends on the specific terms and on how reliably you can pay.

column3: Pay off high-interest credit card debt before investing extra money.
column13: run 1: sec-pay-high-interest-debt + fed-g19-card-rates; run 2: sec-pay-high-interest-debt + fed-g19-card-rates; run 3: fed-g19-card-rates + sec-pay-high-interest-debt
column15: Pay down high-interest credit card debt before putting extra money into investing.
column16: Credit card interest is costly, with an average rate of 21.52% on accounts assessed interest, and few investments can reliably earn that much. Regulator guidance says no investment strategy consistently pays off as well as, or with less risk than, eliminating high interest debt. A few exceptions are commonly noted, such as an employer retirement match or a small emergency cushion, so the order can vary at the edges.

column3: Keep an emergency fund that covers a few months of expenses.
column13: run 1: sec-pay-high-interest-debt; run 2: fed-g19-card-rates; run 3: none
column15: You should keep an emergency fund that covers a few months of living expenses.
column16: Basic consumer finance guidance widely recommends a cash cushion for job loss, medical bills or urgent repairs. It helps you avoid borrowing at high rates when something unexpected happens. The right size varies with your income stability and obligations, so a few months is a common starting range, not a fixed rule.

column3: Renting is throwing money away.
column9: Absolute language; One size fits all
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: none
column15: Paying rent is a waste of money, so owning a home is always the better financial choice.
column16: Rent buys housing, just as a mortgage payment does, so it is not simply lost. Owning builds equity and can bring stability, but it also adds costs like interest, taxes, insurance, repairs and the expense of buying and selling. Whether renting or buying comes out ahead depends on local prices, how long you stay, your savings and your job stability.

column3: Make $5,000 a week from home with my course. Only 10 spots left.
column13: run 1: none; run 2: none; run 3: sec-crypto-guaranteed-returns
column15: A seller says you can earn $5,000 a week from home by buying their course, and that only 10 spots remain.
column16: The post exists to sell a course, and the income figure is the hook that drives the sale. Large, easy earnings from home with no stated work, skills or costs are not what basic consumer finance guidance considers realistic. The limited spots add pressure to pay before you can look into it.
